headline: After Friday's light rain, Saturday brings a brief dry (but foggy, cloudy) break before a Sunday–Monday storm whose uncertain track will decide whether strong winds stay on the coast or reach the Puget Sound and Strait areas.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A weak disturbance brought light rain to the lowlands, including the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore and Puget Sound, and light snow to the mountains Friday, lingering into the late afternoon before things dry out Friday night. With light to calm winds and leftover moisture, fog develops tonight into Saturday morning: dense fog is very likely in the southern interior (70 to 90 percent chance of visibility under a mile) and possible around Puget Sound (25 to 40 percent), especially in river valleys.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday is drier as weak high pressure builds overhead; morning fog clears by afternoon, but skies stay overcast with higher clouds moving in. The high pressure shifts east Sunday, and a developing storm offshore brings rain inland across Western Washington. Parts of Western Washington will likely turn windy by Sunday night, but how windy, and where, depends on the storm's path.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Computer models still disagree on where Monday's low pressure center goes: one major model takes a weakening low into British Columbia, which would keep the strongest winds mostly along the coast, while another brings a deep low ashore toward Western Washington, which would push strong winds into the interior lowlands. By midweek, high pressure is hinted to build and the storm track shifts into California, favoring quieter weather here. The Skokomish River should drop below flood stage Saturday but could rise again next week with more rain; no river flooding is expected elsewhere over the next 7 days.

coast: Coastal flooding remains a threat into the weekend, with the worst expected along the north interior shorelines and lesser impacts elsewhere, and more is possible next week with high astronomical tides, especially Monday. A Coastal Flood Advisory ran until 5 PM Friday for the eastern and western Strait of Juan de Fuca shores (including Sequim and Port Angeles) and until 7 PM Friday for the northern Washington coast and the Grays Harbor County coast. On the water, winds stay light into Saturday morning, then turn easterly Saturday afternoon through Sunday and southeasterly Sunday night, with localized small-craft-advisory-strength gusts possible Saturday night and especially Sunday at the western entrance of the Strait and the southern coastal waters. Monday's storm brings a 75 to 95 percent chance of gale-force gusts over the coastal waters and 40 to 70 percent over the interior waters (including the Strait), plus a 20 to 40 percent chance of storm-force gusts on the coastal waters; seas of 5 to 8 feet this weekend build to 15 to 18 feet Monday, and winds ease Tuesday but stay elevated at times through the week.
watch_for: The track of Monday's storm, which decides whether strong winds stay on the coast or reach the interior lowlands
Dense fog Saturday morning, especially in the southern interior and river valleys
More coastal flooding this weekend and Monday, worst along the north interior shorelines
confidence: Confidence is good in drying tonight and a mostly dry Saturday, but low for Monday's storm because models disagree on its track and strength, with ensembles leaning toward quieter weather by midweek.
